title: Local run ends succeeded after an announced computer_navigate call that produces no result
summary: A channel run announced one surface-owned tool call (computer_navigate), produced no tool result, recorded no operation, and finished succeeded. Root cause: the local runtime replayed its durable bookkeeping and projection rows (MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT, STATE_SNAPSHOT, message.upsert, run.queued, attempt.*, model.usage) to the AG-UI client as protocol events, before the run's RUN_STARTED. The client's verifier rejects a run stream whose first event is not RUN_STARTED or RUN_ERROR, so every local live run died in the browser at its first event. Server-side execution never noticed: the notion tools of the three earlier runs execute in the server process, so their turns completed regardless. The first run whose model chose a browser tool surfaced the dead half: the announced call never reached the surface, nothing executed it, no follow-up run started, and the attempt recorded succeeded.

reproduction.method: Same deployment and stack as the reported run (local mode, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash via the local gateway), a fresh channel, one message inviting a browser action.
reproduction.prompt: Please open https://example.com in your browser and tell me the page title.

browserConsole: [CopilotKit] Error (agent_run_failed_event): AGUIError: First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'
Agent execution failed: AGUIError: First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'
[CopilotKit] Error (agent_run_failed): AGUIError: First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'
observed.transcriptAfterReload: Tool line 'Opened page example.com — Not completed'; status strip 'Run succeeded'.

reproduction.note: The reported run d5bb3cb0 has the same persisted event shape; its live browser session was not captured, but the stream order is deterministic (prepareInput rows always precede RUN_STARTED), so its browser half failed identically.

fix.what: The wire replay emits only the agent's own run envelopes: rows outside a RUN_STARTED..RUN_FINISHED/RUN_ERROR envelope (bookkeeping, input projections, usage, verdicts) never reach the AG-UI client. A state machine rather than one pair of bounds, because a connect replay carries several envelopes back to back. Filtered on rows the page has already read, so the polling read's query count and shape are unchanged.
fix.alternativeRejected: Bounding the envelope inside the store's readReplayPage with two extra queries per poll. That variant passed the new guard but flipped a timing race in the overlapping-runs Stop test (the lease poll fails closed on any error); it was reverted in favor of the zero-query-delta filter.
fix.firstPrinciples: The durable log serves two audiences with different contracts: the history projection (rows of any shape, folded at read time) and the AG-UI wire (protocol-ordered events only). The defect was the conflation; the fix separates them at the presentation boundary rather than by relying on isRecognizedEvent to drop whatever happens to look non-protocol.

guard.whyThisGuard: Every other local-runtime test asserts on persisted rows; none consumed the stream with the real client, which is why a protocol-invalid stream shipped. The guard drives the served endpoint with the real @copilotkit/core client (the exact package the app's locked React SDK imports) and asserts on what that client accepted.
guard.redFirst: On the unfixed tree the guard fails with the production error: AGUIError: First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'; the client owns no tool call.
guard.greenAfterFix: 2 tests, 4 assertions, 0 failures; the client receives the announced call (TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/END) and the assistant text; a second test pins the runner's emitted stream to exactly the eight envelope events.

One test's fixture (bare CUSTOM rows outside any envelope) was updated to the real agent shape: its synthetic events are now wrapped in RUN_STARTED/RUN_FINISHED, and the replay-writer fixture writes the client run id, not the durable run id.
checks.unitTests: bun test tests/local-runtime.test.ts: 8 pass. The fake replay store was updated to the real persisted shape (RUN_STARTED, TEXT rows, RUN_FINISHED); the multi-page cursor expectations are unchanged ([0, 103]).
checks.projectionExhaustive: bun scripts/aooo/projection-exhaustive.ts: 714661 derivation cases and 279620 fold cases, all invariants hold.

liveAcceptance.stack: Local mode restarted with the fix (server PID started 18:11:42; the previously running 17:22:09 server predates the fix and was replaced after stop.sh left it alive and start.sh reused it).
liveAcceptance.prompt: Please open https://example.org in your browser and tell me the page title.

run1.shape: The same persisted shape as the reported run: prepareInput rows, then RUN_STARTED, one line of text, TOOL_CALL_START computer_navigate, RUN_FINISHED; no TOOL_CALL_RESULT; attempt succeeded.

run2.shape: The continuation the surface opens holding the executed tool's result: RUN_STARTED, answer text, RUN_FINISHED.

observed: The browser console shows no AGUIError for the whole turn.
The tool tile reads 'Browsed 1 page' (the pre-fix transcript read 'Not completed').
The computer sidebar shows the live screen and 'The Bot has control'.
The model's answer quotes the real page: 'The page title is "Example Domain" — I read that from the page after opening https://example.org in my browser.'
The folded thread history holds all four turns: user, assistant intent, tool result {ok:true,...untrusted envelope...}, assistant answer; a reload renders the full transcript.
local_messages shows the tool result row between the intent and the answer.
liveAcceptance.transient: A 'Couldn't load earlier messages' notice appeared once mid-turn in both the pre-fix and post-fix sessions; it clears on reload and the durable readback is complete. Recorded as an unexplained transient, not part of this fix.

expectationNote: The issue's expectation (an announced call either records a TOOL_CALL_RESULT and a local_operations row, or the run reports a failure) holds for server-executed governed tools. A surface-owned computer call is answered by the surface: the result enters the thread as the continuation run's input and the folded history records it; computer actions are audited by the computer gateway, not local_operations. A run that announces one and ends succeeded is the protocol's mid-turn state, not a failure, provided the surface executes it and the follow-up run follows, which the live acceptance shows.
